title: Rapid admission-smoothing and probe-scaling playbook to arrest sustained GPU queue growth
creator: Maya Chen
description: After multiple hosted API capacity exhaustion events in regions eu-west-1 and us-west-2, we've observed long-tailed queue growth driven by a combination of bursty tenant traffic patterns, aggressive prefetch behavior, and slow autoscaler probe response. This ticket consolidates follow-up actions: implement a short-term admission-smoothing layer, add rapid-scale probing (fast probes that avoid overcommit), and operationalize a playbook to detect and mitigate 'burst-train' queue reinforcement before pools lock into saturated states.
acceptance_criteria: Controlled admission smoothing reduces median queue growth rate by >= 50% within N minutes under synthetic burst tests
Rapid-scale probe reduces time-to-allocated-capacity by >= 30% in staging without causing oscillatory overscale in 95th percentile of probes
Playbook steps present, tested, and linked from incident Slack runbook; on-call engineer can execute de-escalation in < 10 minutes
No regression to tail latency SLO (>99th pct token latency) in canary region after rollouts
steps_taken: 03/10: Consolidated postmortem notes from last three incidents and extracted common failure modes: (1) burst-train amplification from prefetch + queued warmup, (2) autoscaler probe cooldown too long, (3) admission gating too binary leading to fanout to fallback pools causing imbalance.

03/11: Ran controlled workload generator in staging to reproduce queue spiral. Identified that prefetch jobs (prefetch window 6s) and long tail requests cause KV cache churn increasing per-request cost by ~18%.

03/12: Implemented a lightweight admission smoothing prototype (leaky-bucket based) in front of GPU pool; measured queue growth slope decreased by 42% in synthetic tests. Prototype toggled via feature flag.

03/13: Implemented rapid-scale probe flow: when queue slope > threshold, emit a series of small probe launches to determine available capacity without immediate full-scale decisions. Safe-guarded with backoff and histogram-based rate limiting to avoid probe storms.
03/13: Created initial GitHub PR with admission smoother and probe orchestration: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2345 (performance tests attached).

03/14: Ran a 6-hour soak in staging with cross-tenant mix; observed reduced tail amplification but saw ~3% increase in token-level cost due to smaller probes causing marginal underutilization; flagged for follow-up optimization.
test_plan: Unit tests for admission smoothing (leaky-bucket, token refill, tenant fairness) added and passing
Integration test: simulate 500 tenants with burst patterns (Pareto-distributed interarrival) and verify queue slope metric and latency SLOs
Chaos test: randomly drop probe responses to ensure graceful fallback to existing autoscaler behavior
Canary rollout in eu-west-1 with 5% traffic, monitor queue_slope, pool_utilization, token-cost and 99th_pct_token_latency for 48 hours
next_steps: Complete PR review and merge with feature-flag gating (owner: Diego) — target: 2025-03-15
Tune probe sizing algorithm to reduce token-cost regression: evaluate adaptive probe size based on recent per-tenant batch sizes
Add an automated incident condition to Console: if queue_slope > X and pool_utilization > Y for > 3m, trigger playbook and open ENG hot incident
Document runbook play by step and add toggles for immediate emergency offload to dedicated-eviction pool
Measure cross-region failover impact when smoothing is enabled to ensure no tenant starvation across availability zones
comments: 2025-03-10 Maya Chen: Initial triage complete. Root causes point to interaction between prefetch window and autoscaler probe cadence. Raising P0 because multiple customers experienced degraded response times during the window.

2025-03-11 Diego Alvarez: Reproduced burst-train locally. Prefetch causes KV cache churn; adding a short TTL to prefetch cache items reduced per-request cost. However TTL causes more cold starts — trade-off documented.
2025-03-12 Priya Nair (SRE): Suggest adding a transient admission token so that tenants experiencing bursts are slowed proportionally rather than fully blocked. Will help fairness across tenants.
2025-03-13 Diego Alvarez: Merged initial telemetry for queue_slope and probe_success_rate into Console. These metrics will be used by the incident rule. See Grafana link.
2025-03-14 Erica Song (PM): Prioritize probe-cost tuning in the next cycle; customers care about both availability and token cost — include product criteria in acceptance for next PR.
2025-03-14 On-call: Did a dry run of the playbook against a staged saturation; manual mitigation reduced recovery time from ~22m to ~9m. We need to automate the detection -> mitigation path.
